title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: G is the dual graph of a stable curve, i.e. a boundary stratum M_G of the moduli of curves. A is the set of edges (nodes) and Â the set of oriented edges, i.e. branches at the nodes. For each branch a in Â, T_a is a circle: the unit circle of the tangent line of that branch at the node. E_a, a subset of T_a, is a pair of antipodal points; σ_a swaps them. For an unoriented edge, T_a is the circle of the tensor product of the two branch tangent lines.

The previous page defines S_0T_G. It is the fundamental groupoid of the torus P = ∏_{a∈Â} T_a = (S^1)^Â, restricted to the finite set of base points SE_G = ∏ E_a, which has 2^{|Â|} elements. It is presented using generators u_{α,ξ} (simultaneous counterclockwise half-turns in the coordinates where α_a = -1) and the cocycle n(α,β) ∈ Z^Â, which counts the full turns. That cocycle uses the Z^Â-structure (the π_1 of the torus).

This page gives a second, 'elementary' presentation of S_0T_G:
- Objects: ξ ∈ SE_G.
- Generators: u_{a,ξ}: ξ → σ_aξ, a counterclockwise half-turn in the single coordinate a.
- Relation (1), from the previous page: commuting squares u_{b,σ_aξ}u_{a,ξ} = u_{a,σ_bξ}u_{b,ξ} for a ≠ b.
- Relation (2): the full loops v^a_ξ = u_{a,σ_aξ}∘u_{a,ξ} at ξ commute pairwise for fixed ξ.

The claim is that this presented groupoid is canonically isomorphic to S_0T_G. Topologically this is the edge-path groupoid of the product CW structure on (S^1)^Â, where each circle has 2 vertices and 2 edges. The 1-cells are the u_{a,ξ}. The 2-cells e_a × e_b (with fixed vertex in the other coordinates) are exactly the squares (1). Since π_1 of the 2-skeleton equals π_1 of the torus, the claim is correct.

He then says the same construction with A in place of Â, i.e. E_G = ∏_{a∈A} E_a ⊂ P_G = ∏_{a∈A} T_a, gives a groupoid _0T_G with fundamental group Z^A, written multiplicatively. This yields a commutative square:
- top row: S_0T_G → ST_G;
- bottom row: _0T_G → T_G;
- vertical maps: induced by multiplication T_{a'} × T_{a''} → T_a (on π_1, the summation Z^Â → Z^A).

The horizontal arrows embed these local 'torus' groupoids, attached to the stratum M_G, into the full Teichmüller groupoids with tangential base points at the boundary.

Purpose: to describe combinatorially the local contribution of a boundary stratum, namely the circle bundle of normal smoothing directions (essentially the fiber of the real oriented blow-up), to the Teichmüller groupoid. This is a step toward a generators-and-relations description of the Teichmüller tower from Esquisse d'un programme. The next page begins the case of modular dimension 1 (M_{0,4} and M_{1,1}).
errors: Relation (2) is redundant. Commutation of the full loops v^a_ξ, v^b_ξ follows from the four squares (1) at ξ, σ_aξ, σ_bξ, σ_aσ_bξ, because the 2-skeleton of the product cell structure already has the π_1 of the torus. This is harmless, not wrong.
Notation slip: the diagram writes aξ and a^2ξ for σ_aξ and σ_a^2ξ.
The phrase 'de groupe fondamental Z^A' for _0T_G is meant locally: the vertex groups are Z^A. The groupoid itself has 2^{|A|} objects and is connected.

ideas.what: Presentation of the fundamental groupoid of the torus (S^1)^n on the 2^n base points {±1}^n. Generators are half-turns in each coordinate; relations are commuting squares (plus redundant commutation of the full loops).
ideas.modern_name: Edge-path groupoid presentation of π_1 of a product CW complex (cubical structure on the torus)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Brown, groupoid van Kampen; classical CW topology)

ideas.what: Local model of the Teichmüller groupoid at a boundary stratum M_G: a torus of tangent or smoothing directions, one circle per branch (Â) or per node (A). Base points are discrete antipodal 'real' directions, and there is a Z^Â- or Z^A-structure given by twists.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points at maximal or partial degeneration; fibers of the Kato–Nakayama / real oriented blow-up of the boundary of the moduli of curves; Dehn twists as π_1 of the normal torus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara–Nakamura; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Bakalov–Kirillov (Lego–Teichmüller); Kato–Nakayama (log spaces)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches the Teichmüller tower and base points 'at infinity' but not this explicit construction

ideas.what: Comparison square between the branch-wise version (S, indexed by Â) and the node-wise version (indexed by A), induced by T_{a'} × T_{a''} → T_{a'} ⊗ T_{a''}.
ideas.modern_name: Tensor-product map of normal directions at a node (the smoothing parameter t = xy); summation Z^Â → Z^A on twist lattices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in deformation theory of nodal curves (Deligne–Mumford)

missed.claim: Grothendieck works explicitly with a 'doubled' Teichmüller groupoid ST_G: base points are tangent directions at both branches of each node, with half-turn generators in each branch separately. Its relation to the usual groupoid (base point in the tensor product) is given by a comparison square. Half-turns on single branches, distinct from half-twists of the Dehn twist, are not standard generators in the Lego–Teichmüller literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a refined discrete base-point system, 2^{|Â|} points per stratum, that may make the Galois action on Teichmüller groupoids with real-direction tangential base points easier to bookkeep. This is only mildly new; it resembles existing tangential-base-point formalisms.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a correct but routine presentation of the fundamental groupoid of a torus on a finite set of base points. It serves Grothendieck's local description of Teichmüller groupoids at boundary strata. The branch-wise 'S' variant is a minor unpublished detail; the underlying ideas (tangential base points, twist lattices) are well established in the literature.
transcription_corrections: In the diagram, 'aξ' and 'a^2ξ = ξ' are Grothendieck's abbreviation for σ_aξ and σ_a^2ξ = ξ.
The line 'Prenant T_G [en fonction] de S_0T_G' plausibly reads 'Prenant T_G au lieu de S_0T_G' (taking T_G instead of S_0T_G), with 'au lieu' partly struck.
The struck word after 'une construction' may be 'analogue'.
In the final square, the right-hand entries carry a superscript decoration in the image (something like S𝒯_G^♯ and 𝒯_G^♯) that is omitted in the transcription.
'défini Z^A' in the left margin: the line reads roughly 'de groupe fondamental … Z^A, décrit multiplicativement, défini comme S_0T_G à partir de E_G'.
